page: Microsoft Azure FX32mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and int8 operations. The instance contains 672 GB of system memory, establishing a generous allocation of 21 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed via an integrated 1,890 GB local NVMe SSD, while discrete GPU acceleration is absent.

Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core compute capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2,313.0 and strong multi-core scoring at 18,003.0. The server demonstrates exceptional text processing and encryption throughput, complemented by strong uncached memory bandwidth reaching 232.79 GB/s for reads and 136.78 GB/s for writes. Compression benchmarks remain strong, achieving 34.68 GB/s in single-threaded gzip and 200.05 GB/s in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Static web serving throughput reaches 49.05 GB/s. For machine learning inference, prompt processing and small-model generation perform strongly, though generation throughput on large 70B parameter models falls into the lower performance quartile due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX32mds_v2 delivers substantial compute density and memory capacity per core, eliminating the need to scale out to higher vCPU tiers merely to satisfy memory footprints. The bundled NVMe SSD provides low-latency local scratch space, offsetting external disk overheads. This architecture is optimal for memory-bound enterprise applications, electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory caching systems, large relational database backends, and data transformation pipelines requiring sustained clock speeds.
